articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed; avg 12 published per cycle (63 vs 56 yesterday); 1 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05) bars a new one. Nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: Multi-source fell to 17% (11 of 63), its third straight drop (28 → 25 → 17) and 13 points under target. The day grew by seven stories, and the extra ones were single-outlet picks, many of them China tech and economy items from Zhidx, TMTPost and SCMP and science items from one journal outlet each. US datelines rose to 27%, two points over the ceiling.
watching: Hormuz: mines hitting tankers, Gulf pipelines rerouting exports past the strait, and Iran weighing a Qatari plan, with Vance writing to Rezaei.
The European Central Bank: Lagarde leaving early while the bank faces opposing shocks, as commodity prices rise 23% and copper premiums hit a record.
Pentagon churn: Hegseth firing General Sylvia, a Chinook crash in Bosnia killing four, and Japan agreeing to assemble US missiles.
Yemen, with 281,000 displaced, and Gaza going into winter with its solar power fading under the siege.
Cyclone Arnab over Andhra Pradesh, and bandits killing 60 in Taraba, Nigeria.
Maduro's New York case losing its judge as the Venezuela talks move into court.
coverageGaps: Multi-source hit 17%, the lowest in the recent window. Most single-outlet stories are tech, crypto (CoinDesk) and China business.

Eleven datelines name a country, not a city (United States ×6, China ×2, Switzerland ×2, Israel), up from six yesterday. The missing-dateline metric does not catch them, and mobile's dateline strip needs exact city names.
One science story is crypto from CoinDesk (Fewer Qubits Threaten Bitcoin), so CoinDesk is counted as a science source. The science count of 8 overstates the science desk by one.
Two stories rest only on state media or advocacy outlets (the Putin Africa summits story from TASS, and the Gaza solar story), labelled in the body. One story was quarantined.
context: Output rose to 63 across five completed cycles, with a 0.1-day freshness median, six regions, and no outlet above 8%. Science reached 8 and sci-tech made up 35%. The pause holds until 2026-11-05 while the stage runner cuts over, so the multi-source slide and the country-only datelines are recorded for the operator rather than acted on. The datelines are a writer-prompt question, and no tunable parameter covers them.
